name: MinutesLink
tagline: Calendar-connected meeting recorder with summaries and searchable notes

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 10 AI-processed calls per month; pricing card caps each call at 30 minutes.
tiers.notes: A separate official FAQ says 60 minutes per call, so the vendor's own public pages conflict; this records the stricter pricing-card limit.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 30 calls per monthly cycle or 360 calls per annual cycle; unlimited recording storage and concurrent meetings.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 100 calls per monthly cycle or 1,200 calls per annual cycle; unlimited recording storage and concurrent meetings.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 AI-processed calls per month; pricing card says 30 minutes per call, while an official FAQ says 60.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to 47% lower annually); plan copy says billed at renewal or when the call limit is reached
pricing.hiddenCosts: The pricing page says subscriptions can be billed 'upon limit,' implying early rebilling when the included call allowance is exhausted, but it does not publish a separate overage rate.

verdictSummary: The visible meeting notes loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. MinutesLink earns its keep through capture, integrations, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private meeting notes pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: local Whisper model or optional API key in .env
whatYouLose: calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness
whyPeopleStillPay: MinutesLink: Customers pay for automatic capture, dependable speaker handling, search across calls, and notes arriving without manual file wrangling.
ongoingBurden: Own audio capture permissions, diarization quality, model downloads, storage, privacy, and integrations.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

alternatives.name: Fathom
alternatives.desc: A hosted free recorder with calendar plumbing, unlimited transcripts, basic summaries and search.

facts.install: Hosted signup, connect Google or Outlook Calendar, and install or authorize Fathom's meeting capture app or bot
facts.engines: Fathom's proprietary AI plus third-party subprocessors including Anthropic, OpenAI and Google; individual model names are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Meeting audio/video, transcripts, notes and calendar/attendee metadata in Fathom's US-hosted cloud; recordings remain until deleted on free plans and can be downloaded or exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free tier provides only a small number of advanced summaries each month, so structured notes and action-item extraction quickly become paid.
facts.setupBlocker: Authorizing calendar, microphone or screen capture and the visible meeting bot or beta bot-free recorder

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: Google Calendar, local recording, structured notes and searchable history in one Mac app.

facts.install: Download the notarized macOS app, move it to Applications, grant audio/accessibility permissions and download an on-device model
facts.engines: Local ASR includes Parakeet, Nemotron, Cohere Transcribe, Whisper via WhisperKit, Qwen3 ASR, SenseVoice, Indic ASR and experimental Gemma; summaries use OpenAI, OpenRouter, ChatGPT OAuth or local Ollama
facts.dataFormat: Recordings, dictation history, transcripts, notes and model caches in local macOS app storage; optional iCloud sync sends text but not audio, and optional summary providers receive transcript text
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Apple-Silicon/macOS-only and the desktop app must be running, so it cannot replace a cross-platform calendar bot for a team.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple Silicon and several macOS permissions are mandatory; first use needs a model download, and cloud-quality summaries need an API key, ChatGPT login or local Ollama

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: Calendar-aware meeting capture, summaries and a searchable local archive without sending a bot.

facts.install: Install the signed macOS DMG, Windows EXE or Linux package, grant audio/accessibility permissions and choose local, cloud or BYOK processing
facts.engines: Local Whisper via whisper.cpp; NVIDIA Parakeet and Nemotron via sherpa-onnx; local LLMs via llama.cpp; BYOK OpenAI, Groq, xAI, Mistral, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, Corti, Anthropic/Google and OpenWhispr Cloud
facts.dataFormat: Notes and history in local SQLite with recordings/model caches in app directories; optional sync uses OpenWhispr Cloud/Neon PostgreSQL, while cloud or BYOK audio goes to the selected provider
facts.gapVsPaid: Calendar-to-capture automation is narrower, and desktop audio permissions and routing can fail where a managed meeting bot would simply join.
facts.setupBlocker: Meeting capture needs OS audio permissions and a model download or cloud/API choice; macOS also needs Accessibility and Screen Recording/System Audio permission

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of MinutesLink is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for MinutesLink, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + whisper.cpp + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private meeting notes pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: calendar and CRM integrations; cross-call team analytics; calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
